gap: No result ChatGPT got states how one tank compares with one battery charge: a Honda EU2200i gets 3,645 Wh from 0.95 gal at quarter load (450 W × 8.1 h). That is about 3.9 full drains of a 1 kWh station (BLUETTI Elite 100 V2, 946 Wh measured) and costs about $1.01/kWh in gas at today's $3.87/gal, against $0.19 to refill the battery from the grid.
standout_why: ChatGPT's search returned no results and its answer cited no pages, so there were no rival pages to compare against. Its own answer gives only the battery side ('a 1,000Wh power station might run a 100W appliance for roughly 8–9 hours'). It never puts a number on the generator side: no Wh per tank, no cost per kWh, no hours at the same load and no Wh per lb. Its table only says 'Can refuel for extended use' and lists a 'Typical cost' range.
decides: It confirms the pick and makes it a number. At the same 450 W load, a 1 kWh station runs about 2.1 h, while one 0.95 gal tank in the generator runs 8.1 h and weighs less per Wh carried (76.9 vs 41.0 Wh/lb). For outages longer than a few hours or for heavy loads, the generator wins. For short outages, indoor use and cheap energy, the station wins: grid recharge costs about $0.18/kWh against about $1.01/kWh for gas at quarter load. The roughly 4-to-1 tank-to-charge ratio is the single figure a shopper can use to choose.
